data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Neyam' meaning 'nectar'. This name is associated with the goddess of knowledge and wisdom, Saraswati. The name 'Neysa' symbolizes the sweetness and purity of knowledge and the wisdom it imparts. The name Neysa carries the meaning “Nectar, Sweet” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Neysa usually hope their child will grow to embody nectar, sweet and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Neysa is mentioned as the capital of the Vedic civilization during the Rigvedic period, around 1500-1000 BCE. It is described as a sacred and prosperous city, known for its commerce, learning and religious importance.

Later historical references suggest that Neysa may have been identified with the ancient Indian city of Hastinapura, which was the capital of the Pandava and Kuru kingdoms mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata. This identification is based on similarities in the descriptions of the two cities, such as their religious significance and prosperity.
